note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address and lighting answer below comes from one City of Huntington Beach page, its Park Amenities list, where the pickleball block is four lines long and its heading settles the lighting for all four parks at once. The City's Tennis & Pickleball Information page adds the community-centre addresses and the hours of the lighted tennis courts, which belong to tennis and not to these. Where the City is silent, on hours, on price, on surface, on parking, this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking:
Huntington Beach publishes nothing about parking at any of these four parks. The word does not appear in the pickleball block of the City's Park Amenities page, which gives each venue one line: a name, a street address and a count. It does not appear on the Tennis & Pickleball Information page either.

The same amenities page does name three of the four parks under "CITY PARKS WITH A RESTROOM": Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park. Boardwalk Park is not on that list, and that is recorded here as a silence rather than a no. The planning fact that matters more than parking is light. The City states that none of these courts is lit, so every visit is a daylight visit.
slots.peak_hours:
The City publishes no hours for its pickleball courts, no busy periods, no rotation rule and no league night. What it publishes instead is a heading that does the work of a schedule: "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". A weekday evening game is possible here in June and not in December.

The trap to avoid is the tennis page. It lists lighted tennis courts at Edison and Marina, at the same street addresses as two of the pickleball venues, open "Dusk to 10 p.m. nightly". Those lines sit under the heading "Lighted Tennis Courts & Handball/Racquetball Courts" and do not apply to the pickleball courts.
slots.surface_condition:
The City names no surface anywhere in its pickleball record. Each venue gets one line on the Park Amenities page, and that line holds a name, an address and a number of courts. There is no word for what the courts are made of, whether they are dedicated or painted onto something else, or how they are kept.

The page does show that pickleball is counted separately from tennis. Edison Park and Marina Park appear under both headings; Worthy Park and Boardwalk Park appear under pickleball and not under tennis. Whether the pickleball courts at Edison or Marina share ground with the tennis courts is something the City does not say.
slots.local_scene:
Thirteen verified courts across four City parks, none of them lit, and every one of them stated in a single four-line block on the City's Park Amenities page. Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park hold four courts each; Boardwalk Park holds one. Nothing was refused.

The distinctive fact about this city is what it says no to. Huntington Beach adds four stated negatives in one heading, more than the directory previously held in prose, and it is the first city here where the operator states that no published court is lit.

What the City does not say is nearly everything else. It publishes no hours, no price, no surface, no parking and no indoor or outdoor answer. Its Tennis & Pickleball Information page prices reserved tennis courts and never prices or frees a pickleball court, which is why Huntington Beach is not recorded as free. That same page is where organised pickleball appears: OC Racquet Sports offers clinics, camps and private lessons the City describes in terms of "tennis or pickleball goals".

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most park around the courts
best_for.text: Edison Park has four pickleball courts, unlit, and appears on more of the City's amenity lists than any other pickleball park in Huntington Beach: restroom, basketball court, handball court, skate park, sports field, tennis courts, volleyball court and walking loop. The Edison Community Center is at the same address and takes registrations for the City's tennis and pickleball programmes.

best_for.heading: Best if you want four courts and no tennis courts alongside
best_for.text: Worthy Park has four pickleball courts, unlit, and is the one four-court venue the City does not list under its tennis heading, so nothing lit at this park competes for attention. The City lists a restroom, a basketball court, a picnic table or shelter, a sports field and a walking loop, and gives the park two addresses; 1831 17th St. is the one paired with the count.

best_for.heading: Best if you are four players who want one court
best_for.text: Boardwalk Park has one pickleball court, unlit, in a park the City lists for an exercise course and a volleyball court and nothing else. One court is one game at a time with no rotation, which suits a group that arrives together and does not suit anyone hoping to find a game. Daylight only, on the City's own statement.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Huntington Beach have?
faqs.a: Thirteen, across four City parks: four each at Edison Park, Marina Park and Worthy Park, and one at Boardwalk Park. No venue was refused. The City lists no other park with a pickleball court, so thirteen is both the verified count and the City's own total.

faqs.q: Are any of the courts lit?
faqs.a: No, and the City says so rather than leaving it to be inferred. The heading over all four venues reads "CITY PARKS WITH A PICKLEBALL COURT (NO LIGHTING)". Huntington Beach is the first city on this site where the operator states that no published court is lit, so every court here closes with the daylight.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Huntington Beach?
faqs.a: Not stated, so this page does not say so. The City prices reserved tennis courts, "$9 per hour" on its tennis page and "$4 per hour" in a separate block on its amenities page, and never prices or frees a pickleball court. Silence on price is recorded as unknown, not as free.

faqs.q: Why does Worthy Park have two addresses?
faqs.a: Because the City publishes two. Its amenities page pairs the court count with 1831 17th St., and its Tennis & Pickleball Information page lists "Worthy Park 1801 Main Street" among the community centres that take registrations. The count-bearing address is the one published here, and the other is stated on the venue page rather than dropped.
